title: No Proof for Dog-Trade Defenses: Demand Quarantine and Abolition
excerpt: Claims about tradition and farm-raised dogs cannot replace transport records, quarantine proof, or protection for stolen companions. Vietnam needs transparent enforcement and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Families cannot protect companions from theft, disease, or illicit transport with slogans. Claims that dogs in trade are farm-raised or that custom settles the matter require records: lawful origin, vaccination, quarantine, transport, and inspection. None of those claims can be treated as proof without documentation.

Tradition does not verify supply

Tradition cannot establish where an animal came from. Farm-raised claims cannot establish lawful origin. A credible system needs traceable ownership, veterinary records, quarantine controls, and inspection at every stage. Where operators evade those safeguards, regulators face a biosecurity gap—and families face the loss of companions to theft.

Rabies makes delay dangerous

Rabies exposure usually occurs when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Treatment must begin before symptoms develop. WHO guidance sets out these facts.

Household exposure incidents and commercial dog-trade supply chains are separate dimensions of broken biosecurity. One does not prove the other caused it. Both demand accountable prevention, veterinary quarantine, and enforcement against illegal transport.

Vietnamese communities can close the gap

Vietnamese families, rescuers, veterinarians, and local reformers can demand a system that protects people and pets. State rabies-control targets are not the same as SDE’s campaign demand: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
